source.text: Particle 7 of the 2000 drawn with the seed 20261016 from the population of examples/synthetic-triso-population.json: the thinnest SiC layer of the 2000 (SiC 30.64 um). The drop across the porous carbon buffer, from its inner face to its outer face: P / (4 pi k) x (1/r_in - 1/r_out) = 13.4277 K for P = 66.5051 mW. The observed value is the difference of FEED's two face temperatures of the buffer (the kernel's surface from the interface of two cells, the buffer's outer face from the gap's patch value). Tolerance 0.15 K = 0.5 % of the 17.868 K internal rise + the mesh bound 5 x 3.537 K / 48^2 = 0.0077 K + the wedge of the solver's mesh (the 2 degree wedge of the sphere with its radii times lambda = 0.999695, 48 cells in every region), which makes every drop lambda^2 = 0.999391 of the sphere's, rounded up to 0.05 K, fixed before any run.
source.check: Second method: FEED's own closed form (src/core/trisoSolve.ts, tests/seedOracleTriso.test.ts, to 1e-6 K) and FEED's finite-volume solution; the real solver (FEED_SOLVER=1, tests/seedOracleTriso.test.ts) with every check of the run passing, and its saved output (tests/golden/seed-oracles-triso/) inside the tolerance.
